title: GDL-69A FIS - DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION
question: How does the GDL-69A satellite data link improve weather coverage compared to land-based transmissions?
answer: The GDL-69A Flight Information System  is a remote-mounted component of the Garmin G 1000 avionics system. The GDL-69A gives weather and FIS information to the pilot. The information is controlled and seen through the Multi-Function Display . Information is sent from the data link receiver to the MFD through the high-speed data bus ethemet data path. With a current subscription, XM satellite radio service is available with the GDL-69A. The signals that the data link receives from satellites give better coverage than land-based transmissions. The XM radio is tuned through the MFD. Analog audio is sent to the audio panel and shares the AUX music input with the external audio entertainment input. NEXRAD Radar Coverage  Surface Analysis with City ForecastsThe GDL-69A XM Weather Data Link is the receiver for the FIS, and is installed behind the instrument panel. It is a remote sensor.The CI-2480 antenna for the GDL-69A FIS is installed on the left upper surface of the fuselage at FS 65.33.
